title: runtime/scheduler: add starvation guardrails + metrics for long-queue fairness
author: Marcus Reed
body:
Title: Add starvation guardrails (max wait bound, periodic long-queue service) and metrics to detect starvation

Context
This PR builds on the two-queue prototype dispatch policy (short/interactive vs long/prefill-heavy) landed in #8433 and the classification plumbing in #8427.

In mixed workloads we saw cases where continuous short traffic can keep the short queue non-empty for long periods (esp. under burst + batching), causing long requests to accumulate and experience unbounded wait. This is the exact failure mode SRE called out in the design review: we need explicit, measurable starvation/fairness guarantees and signals for canary.

What this PR does
1) Starvation guardrails in scheduler dispatch
- Adds a max-wait bound (soft) for the long queue. If the oldest long request has been waiting longer than a configurable threshold, the scheduler will force-service long work even when the short queue is non-empty.
- Adds periodic long-queue service (token/window based) to prevent pathological long starvation under sustained short load.
- Preserves short-first behavior under normal conditions; long service is injected only when fairness thresholds are exceeded.

2) Guardrail configuration knobs (behind existing feature flag)
- Introduces the following config params (names finalized per review):
  - runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.long_starvation_max_wait_ms (default: 2000ms)
  - runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.long_service_interval_ms (default: 250ms)
  - runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.long_service_burst (default: 1)  // how many long dequeues to allow when guardrail triggers
- All knobs are only read when runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled=true (default-off).

3) Metrics to detect starvation / fairness regressions
- Adds per-class queue wait time histograms:
  - redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_ms{class=short|long}
- Adds counters for forced long service:
  - redwood_runtime_scheduler_long_guardrail_forced_total{reason=max_wait|interval}
- Adds gauge for oldest long wait (sampled at dequeue time):
  - redwood_runtime_scheduler_long_oldest_wait_ms
- Adds a "starvation suspected" counter that increments when oldest long wait exceeds 2x the configured max wait (this is a canary-only signal; not used for control):
  - redwood_runtime_scheduler_long_starvation_suspected_total

Why these guardrails (vs SRPT approximation)
We intentionally keep control logic simple and predictable for the prototype: short-first with explicit fairness injection. SRPT-like schemes are more sensitive to estimation error (prefill prediction), which we are still iterating on. The guardrails here are designed to be robust even when classification is imperfect.

Implementation notes
- The scheduler maintains per-class FIFO queues and tracks enqueue timestamp for each request.
- The fairness logic is evaluated at dispatch selection time:
  - If long queue empty => short (existing behavior)
  - Else if short queue empty => long (existing behavior)
  - Else if oldest long wait >= long_starvation_max_wait_ms => service long (forced, reason=max_wait)
  - Else if now - last_long_service_ts >= long_service_interval_ms => service long (forced, reason=interval)
  - Else => service short (default)
- We explicitly cap forced servicing via long_service_burst to avoid draining long and harming interactive SLOs during sudden long backlog.

Testing
- Unit tests covering:
  - Max-wait triggers long service even under continuous short arrivals
  - Interval-based service fires at expected cadence
  - long_service_burst cap is respected
  - Metrics emitted on forced paths and normal paths
- Microbench sanity (local): no measurable overhead in the dispatch hot-path beyond an extra timestamp comparison (~1-2ns in the synthetic loop).

Operational / rollout
- No behavior change unless the mixed workload scheduler feature flag is enabled.
- These metrics will be used by upcoming dashboard PRs to set canary alerts around long starvation.

Related
- Linear: ENG-4823 (two-queue policy), ENG-4824 (metrics), ENG-4831 (fairness validation)
- Prior PR: #8433

Commits (squash summary)
- runtime/scheduler: track enqueue timestamps and oldest long wait
- runtime/scheduler: implement max-wait and interval fairness injection
- runtime/metrics: add wait histograms + forced service counters
- tests: add starvation guardrail unit tests
- docs/comments: document config knobs and invariants

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/mixed_workload_dispatch.cc
- runtime/scheduler/queue.h
- runtime/metrics/scheduler_metrics.cc
- runtime/config/runtime_scheduler_flags.yaml
- runtime/tests/scheduler/mixed_workload_starvation_test.cc

Reviewer discussion (selected)
- Sofia: requested clearer semantics on whether max-wait is hard vs soft bound. Resolution: documented as a soft bound (scheduler attempts to service long once threshold exceeded; actual completion still depends on GPU service time / batch formation).
- Lena: flagged risk that interval-based service could oscillate under bursty traffic. Resolution: added long_service_burst and ensured last_long_service_ts only updates on actual long dequeue.
- Omar: asked to align metric naming with existing runtime metrics conventions. Resolution: renamed from scheduler_long_wait_ms to redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_ms{class=...} and added the forced_total counter with reason labels.
- Sean (SRE): requested an explicit "suspected starvation" signal for paging experiments. Resolution: added long_starvation_suspected_total (not used in control loop) and noted it should be used only during canary.

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- runtime-perf-smoke: PASS
- lint: PASS
- One rerun due to flaky timing assertion in mixed_workload_starvation_test (fixed by using a fake clock / deterministic scheduler time source in test).

Checklist
- [x] Behind feature flag
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Metrics added and names reviewed
- [x] Defaults set to conservative values
- [x] Documentation/comments for knobs and invariants

Merge
Merged via squash into main on 2024-11-09.
